ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Articles 2(2), 2(7), 5-2, and 5-3) as amended through 2024; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Articles 10-2 through 10-6); Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Part V, Articles 19-75 and 289-345 (stock corporation formation); Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Articles 4-5); Financial Services Commission Regulations on Beneficial Ownership Verification and CDD issued through the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate from the Supreme Court Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office / District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued in an Apostille Convention state: official issuance -> notarization (if required) -> Hague Apostille by the competent central authority of the issuing country; no consular legalization. For non-Apostille states: official issuance -> notarization -> Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification -> Korean Embassy/Consulate legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Current Corporate Registration Particulars (Deungsabon equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (local district court registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route for any onward cross-border use in an Apostille member state; consular legalization only if the receiving authority is in a non-member state. For domestic Korean use, no apostille is needed; the certified registry copy itself is accepted by banks and tax authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Irrevocable Power of Attorney for Foreign Parent Company Signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of the foreign parent company / Korean Notary Public for matching Korean-language signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Origin notarization -> Hague Apostille by the designated central authority of the parent company's home jurisdiction (if apostille member) -> submission to Korean registry/bank; or origin notarization -> foreign ministry certification -> Korean consular legalization (only for non-Apostille states). Never combine apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) for the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public / Notarization Office under the Korean Notary Public Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Articles are prepared in Korean and notarized domestically; if the parent board resolution annexed to the articles is in a foreign language, that annex must follow the apostille route described above and be accompanied by a certified Korean translation. No consular legalization is needed for documents issued inside Korea, except for submission to non-Apostille foreign governments, which is outside this Korean incorporation step.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Parent Company or Principal Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent company's lead bank (bank compliance department or branch manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank statement print or bank letter -> notarization -> Hague Apostille from the home jurisdiction's central authority (if apostille member); for non-member jurisdictions: notarization -> foreign ministry certification -> Korean consular legalization. Korean banks also accept a direct signed SWIFT/ISO 9362 CFO request from the parent bank as an alternative, but the apostilled paper version remains the safest path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Seal Registration and Signature Specimen
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean District Court Registry Office / Corporate Seal Custodian at the company's parent bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Korean issuance requires apostille only when used outside Korea; for the Korean incorporation filing, the seal registration certificate is issued directly by the registry and requires no apostille or consular legalization. Foreign parent seal/signature certificates, if any, must follow the separate apostille or consular path in accordance with member/non-member status.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The formation agent, Korean counsel, and any involved Korean financial institution must screen all ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more of shares, all directors, all officers with statutory authority, and any authorized signatory against the following mandatory lists: (i) Korean Financial Intelligence Unit watchlist and designated proscribed persons; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) FATF blacklist and grey-list publications; (iv) OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists to protect correspondent banking; (v) Financial Supervisory Service prohibited financial-institution lists; (vi) EU and UK sanctions lists; (vii) sanctions and restrictive measures administered by the South Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; and (viii) adverse-media and politically-exposed persons databases covering foreign and domestic PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Screening must use Hangul/English fuzzy matching, aliases, birth-date normalization, passport numbers, and corporate registry identifiers, and must be refreshed before incorporation, before bank account opening, and annually thereafter. Any hit must be escalated immediately to the chief compliance officer and, where warranted, to the Korean FIU as a suspicious transaction report before any corporate action is completed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (IROS) online name search and business registration clearance portal (iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory trade name of a Chusik Hoesa must be registered in Korean Hangul; a foreign-language auxiliary name may be used for public branding but does not replace the Korean statutory name for corporate registration. For foreign investors, a Hangul phonetic transliteration of the foreign name is generally accepted if it is pronounceable in Korean and does not coincide with a pre-existing identical trade name. The four-tier naming convention should be: (1) a distinctive verbal mark or family identifier; (2) a descriptive business-objective element relevant to personal wealth analytics, cloud software, or investment tracking; (3) an optional geographic or corporate-group modifier; and (4) the mandatory legal form suffix Chusik Hoesa. The registry will reject any name that is misleading as to the company's limited liability, is identical to a registered trade name in the same or similar line of business, or contains tokens requiring prior ministerial approval. If the company intends to use English marketing names, such names should be separately registered as trademarks to prevent confusion after incorporation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Trademark-protected slogans where third-party consent is absent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of receiving a written name rejection, the applicant or its Korean counsel must file a written objection with the district court registration officer under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act, stating the grounds of distinctiveness, proprietary character, and legal compliance of the rejected name. Simultaneously, the applicant should file a fresh name-search application using an amended name that either adds a distinctive mark, removes the prohibited token, or changes the phonetic transliteration. If rejection is caused by a prior identical trade name in the same business category, the applicant may submit a consent letter from the prior registrant or modify the name to a non-confusing variant. If rejection is based on a prohibited financial or public token, the company must obtain a written approval or no-objection letter from the Financial Services Commission or the relevant competent ministry before resubmission. The court's written decision on administrative objection must be issued within one month, and a subsequent appeal may be taken to the High Court; all administrative remedies must be exhausted before judicial review. During the appeal, the proposed name should not be used on business stationery, invoices, or advertising.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not categorically prohibited by the Korean Commercial Act for filing the principal office address, but it is operationally and commercially impermissible for this low-risk fintech software business. The National Tax Service and the Financial Supervisory Service apply a substance-over-form standard, requiring actual business premises where records are kept, clients can be met, IT infrastructure is operated, and employees perform their duties. Korean commercial banks, when opening a corporate account for a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa, conduct on-site visits and reject virtual-office addresses as a red flag, particularly where the stated business is financial portfolio tracking and payment rails will include Stripe and Apple IAP. A virtual office may be used as a supplementary administrative address, but the registered office should be a physically leased office, at least one member of local staff should be present during business hours, and the company must be able to produce lease agreements, utility receipts, payroll records, and server access logs upon demand. For tax and bank purposes, virtual office and commercial mailbox are therefore not permissible as the sole principal office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The National Tax Service and municipal government conduct unannounced physical inspections under the Bona Fide Business Place Inspection program, particularly within the first 18 months after incorporation when there are foreign shareholders. The inspection checklist includes: original lease agreement in the company's own name; sufficient floor area for personnel; a physical company signboard; business registration certificate posted; VAT invoices; bank records; payroll and employment insurance declarations; national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident insurance records; software licenses; cloud infrastructure contracts; attendance logs; and directors' presence at the registered office. The quantified risk is approximately 15-25% for a virtual-office-only setup with foreign ownership, and less than 5% where a physical office with at least two local employees and proper corporate records is maintained. A fintech portfolio tracking company additionally faces heightened review because the business model touches payment data and investment-derived income, which may trigger inspection by the Financial Services Commission, the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit, or the National Tax Service if any invoicing anomaly or cross-border payment pattern is detected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, dated January 27, 1962, as most recently amended, particularly Articles 289 (contents of Articles of Incorporation), 290 (share subscription matters), 295 (promoter subscription and payment), 296 (certification of paid-in shares), 317 (registration of incorporation), 318 (effective date of incorporation), 383 (board of directors), 389 (representative director), and 410 (statutory auditor); also the Registration of Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act and its applicable commercial registration provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the local district court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office; for Seoul-based entities this is the Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Office, with online submissions facilitated through the Supreme Court of Korea's I-REG Commercial Registration Information portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Application for Entry of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa) submitted under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation, consent forms of officers, payment certificate for subscribed shares, and proof of registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-in capital is imposed by the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea for a Chusik Hoesa after the removal of the minimum capital requirement. Nevertheless, the entire subscription price for every issued share must be fully paid by the promoters into a domestic commercial bank or securities company account in the name of the company to obtain a statutory payment certificate before incorporation registration. This deposit is not a regulatory blocked escrow account; it is a dedicated incorporation capital deposit account that becomes freely available operating capital only upon successful registration. For the illustrative official state filing fee stated above, a standard paid-in capital of KRW 10,000,000 is assumed; the court filing component and local education surtax vary proportionally with capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA. At the inaugural meeting of the board of directors of [Company Name] Chusik Hoesa (the 'Company'), a stock corporation organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (the 'Act'), duly convened and held on [date] at [time] at the registered office of the Company, the following directors were present in person or by proxy: [director names]. The chairman confirmed that a quorum existed and that the meeting was lawfully called and conducted in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and the Act. After due deliberation, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted. 1. Ratification and Confirmation of Share Capital Subscription. RESOLVED, that the board ratifies and confirms the subscription of the entire issued and outstanding share capital of the Company by the promoters, and confirms that each issued share has been fully paid in cash in accordance with Article 295 of the Act. The board acknowledges the deposit certificate issued by [bank name] evidencing the payment of [currency and amount] into a dedicated incorporation deposit account, and declares that the paid-in capital of the Company is [KRW amount], represented by [number] shares having a par value of [KRW amount] per share. 2. Adoption of Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is hereby established at [full address], and that the lease agreement, occupancy certificate, title deed, or landlord consent regarding that address is approved and adopted. The board authorizes the Representative Director and the Secretary to execute, deliver, and file all documents necessary to register the registered office with the competent Commercial Registration Office and to reflect the registered address in all agreements, tax records, and licenses. 3. Banking Authorization and Signatory Mandate. RESOLVED, that the board authorizes the opening, maintenance, and operation of corporate bank accounts at [bank names], and appoints [name] as the primary signatory and [name] as the joint signatory. Every withdrawal, transfer, deposit instruction, and payment shall be governed by the mandate requiring the primary signatory plus one joint signatory, or such dual authorization protocol as the board may approve from time to time. The banks are hereby directed to honor instruments executed in accordance with this mandate, and the Company shall indemnify the banks for actions taken in reliance upon this resolution. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED, that the following persons are hereby appointed as officers of the Company to serve until the next annual general meeting of shareholders or until succession or removal: [name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [name] as Director and Secretary; and [name] as Statutory Auditor, if required by Article 410 or by the Articles of Incorporation. Each officer accepts the duties incident to the office and is vested with the lawful powers conferred by the Act and the Articles. 5. Execution Authority and Ratification. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director and the Secretary are jointly and severally authorized to prepare, execute, file, and deliver all applications, forms, certificates, consents, tax registrations, business license filings, and correspondence necessary to complete incorporation, corporate registration, tax registration, bank account activation, and industrial or administrative notifications. The Company hereby ratifies and confirms any lawful act previously taken by the promoters or interim directors in connection with the formation of the Company, and authorizes all lawful acts taken pursuant to these resolutions, all to the full extent permitted by law. This resolution is effective as of the date of this meeting and shall remain in full force until repealed by a subsequent board or shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Corporate Bank Account and Officer Signatory Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The designated commercial bank branch named in the First Board Resolution, acting under the bank's corporate account activation and AML/KYC procedures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the designated bank branch the certificate of corporation registration excerpt, the Business Registration Certificate, the corporate seal certificate, the notarized copy of the First Board Resolution, identification documents for all signatories, and proof of the registered office. The bank will perform beneficial ownership checks and source-of-funds checks and will then establish the corporate accounts in the Company name, with the approved dual-signatory or joint authorization mandate. The finance officer should also connect the operating bank account to the Company's Stripe and Apple IAP merchant accounts as part of payment routing. All signatory mandates must match the board resolution, and any later change in officers requires an updated board resolution and bank notification.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate issued by the National Tax Service
Corporate seal certificate and signature specimens
Notarized or certified First Board Resolution
Passport or ID of each authorized signatory and beneficial owner
Completed bank KYC and AML declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional source-of-funds or beneficial ownership information, supply the incorporation deposit certificate, Articles of Incorporation, and the board resolution. If a signatory is rejected, revise the bank mandate by a supplemental board resolution or substitute an approved officer and resubmit the application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the Company is a pure software and cloud-based service under ISIC 6201 with no physical factory, chemical process, assembly line, or warehouse. If the Company later maintains physical equipment, the municipal office of the relevant local government (Si/Gun/Gu) would be the responsible permitting authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, storage, or industrial operating license is triggered by the declared scope of personal wealth analytics and portfolio tracking software. The Company may be required to file a Value-Added Telecommunications Business Report under Article 22 of the Telecommunications Business Act if its cloud platform provides network-based digital services to Korean users, but that is an administrative report and not an industrial operating license. No statutory license is required for the fintech software activity itself, and the target payment rails (Stripe and Apple IAP) do not affect industrial licensing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, with the Korean Environmental Industry and Technology Institute providing technical review assistance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no Full Environmental Impact Assessment, Prior Environmental Review, or Environmental Registration is required for software programming, cloud service delivery, data analytics, or digital portfolio tracking. EIA obligations would only be triggered by a future physical factory, chemical facility, large warehouse, or building construction above the statutory size thresholds under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the Company has no point-source wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emissions, or hazardous waste generation. General office waste disposal must comply with the Waste Control Act, and if the Company ever manages data center equipment, servers, batteries, or electronic waste, it must comply with the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources and any applicable EPR and waste manifest requirements on a per-merchant or per-facility basis; no quantitative N-cy limit applies to the current software-only scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to a purely software-based office; however, the Company's office premises must hold a Fire-Fighting System Completion Inspection report and a fire safety certificate under the Act on Fire Prevention, Installation, and Maintenance of Fire-Fighting Equipment, as issued by the building owner or local fire safety authorities. Occupational health and safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act apply to employees from the date of hiring, and the level of mandatory workplace safety management is based on headcount and the presence of office equipment; no civil defense permit is required for a software-only service entity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act at the local court registry and obtain the certificate of incorporation and corporate registration certificate. Step 2: File an application for business registration with the competent district tax office through HomeTax or in person within 20 days of the commencement of business, or before starting revenue operations where possible. Step 3: Submit the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, proof of business premises, foreign investment report and foreign capital remittance certificate if applicable, and a valid power of attorney for the local representative. Step 4: The district tax office issues a 10-digit Business Registration Certificate; this business registration number functions as both the corporate TIN and the VAT registration number, so no separate VAT identifier is issued. Step 5: A foreign non-resident entity that has not established a Korean branch or Chusik Hoesa but must collect Korean VAT must appoint a Korean tax representative and register through the HomeTax foreign non-resident business registration module; the same 10-digit business registration number is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Korean Chusik Hoesa is a domestic corporation taxed independently under the Corporate Tax Act; no pass-through treatment is available)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box election. Corporate classification follows the Commercial Act and the Corporate Tax Act; there is no domestic hybrid mismatch election available as an elective classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for a Chusik Hoesa; VAT registration is mandatory upon commencement of any taxable business. For individual sole proprietors, annual turnover below KRW 80,000,000 may qualify for the simplified taxpayer regime, but computer programming, software, and digital services under ISIC 6201 are excluded from simplified taxpayer treatment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under Value-Added Tax Act Article 32, VAT-registered business operators must issue electronic tax invoices for all supplies and transmit them to the NTS through HomeTax or a government-approved electronic tax invoice service provider by the day after the supply date. B2C credit/debit card sales are captured automatically from card acquirers and converted into electronic tax invoices by the NTS. There is no continuous fiscal stamping device mandate; anti-fraud control is achieved through mandatory real-time electronic tax invoice transmission, issuance of an NTS digital issuance number, and cross-reconciliation with customs and foreign exchange data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Value-Added Tax Act Article 21 zero-rates exported goods moved from Korea to a foreign destination under a customs export declaration, and exported services including qualifying digital and information technology services where the place of use or performance is shown to be outside Korea and the recipient is a foreign entity or individual without a Korean tax nexus. For this financial portfolio tracking cloud service, the taxpayer should maintain a contract naming the offshore customer, a service invoice denominated in foreign currency, evidence of actual supply and usage outside Korea, and foreign exchange receipt evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration, also known as the Export Declaration Certificate, issued through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system with export declaration number and customs clearance seal for goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for goods
Certificate of Foreign Exchange Receipt or Foreign Currency Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, proving offshore payment proceeds
Electronic tax invoice transmitted to the NTS showing the zero-rated supply

For service exports where no customs declaration exists, substitute the customs bundle with the service contract, detailed service report or usage log, foreign exchange receipt, and evidence demonstrating the offshore place of benefit or use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS audits export zero-rating by cross-checking electronic tax invoices, Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS declarations, and foreign exchange bank receipts. If zero-rating is claimed without valid customs or foreign exchange documentation, the supply is reclassified as taxable at 10% Korean VAT, unpaid VAT is assessed with interest, and additional tax penalties, typically 20% to 40% of the tax amount under the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes, are imposed. In cases of intentional or fraudulent false zero-rating, the NTS may apply a 10-year retrospective reassessment period and refer the matter under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, which carries imprisonment of up to 10 years or fines of up to five times the evaded tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized yet heavily monitored foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA). The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account items, including trade in goods, services, and ordinary business remittances, with minimal formality. In contrast, capital account transactions, such as foreign direct investment, overseas borrowing, and portfolio investment, are subject to ex-ante or ex-post reporting requirements to the Bank of Korea or authorized foreign exchange banks. Since the 2010 reforms, Korea has abolished mandatory surrender requirements for export proceeds; exporters may retain earnings in foreign currency accounts indefinitely, but must report receipt within the statutory reconciliation timeline. Profit remittances, including dividends and liquidation proceeds, are permitted without prior approval once corporate tax and withholding tax obligations are settled and a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate (or its equivalent confirmation) is presented to the paying bank. Non-resident shareholders face statutory withholding rates of up to 22% unless treaty relief is claimed through the appropriate tax residency certificate. The most significant practical hurdle for foreign-owned entities is the requirement to demonstrate the underlying genuine trade or investment purpose for each major FX transaction, as the BOK periodically audits banks for compliance with anti-money laundering and foreign exchange reporting obligations. Additionally, the 'foreign exchange concentration' mechanism restricts pre-announced large conversions above USD 10 million equivalent, requiring simplified but compulsory notice to the BOK. Overall, KRW is not a restricted currency in the official sense, but the documentary burden for capital account movements is substantial, and any deviation from the declared business purpose could trigger civil or criminal penalties for both the entity and its banking counterparty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or fixed conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in South Korea. Under Article 5 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related Regulations, an exporter must collect foreign exchange proceeds within six months from the date of export clearance unless the MOEF approves an extension. Proceeds must be received into a domestic foreign exchange bank account or a registered overseas account, and the receiving bank must report such receipt to the BOK within the prescribed reporting cycle. The exporter may freely hold, sell, or convert KRW without any statutory percentage requirement, subject to the bank's internal FX transaction documentation procedures.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Trade Finance Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital financial institutions and fintech EMI platforms such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex are not licensed to provide local KRW current accounts or IBAN-equivalent accounts in South Korea. The Banking Act ascribes deposit-taking activities to authorized banks only, and the FSC does not permit non-bank EMIs to use a sponsor-bank arrangement in a manner that effectively creates an independent multi-currency account for a Korean domestic entity. Such EMIs may be used only as ancillary payment gateways for cross-border payables where funds are ultimately routed through a licensed Korean bank account. However, this introduces an unnecessary layer of regulatory friction for a software company that needs to settle local payroll and VAT obligations. Therefore, the only viable compliance path is to open a primary operational account at a Tier-1 domestic bank and to use recognized merchant acquirers for card payment settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Chusik Hoesa with foreign directors, physical presence in a South Korean bank branch is mandatory. Under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act and the financial institution's internal KYC policies, the registered director or the attorney-in-fact with a valid Korean Alien Registration Card (ARC) must appear in person for corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for the initial banking relationship, although post-onboarding banking services may be managed through online corporate banking portals. If the foreign director does not possess an ARC, the bank may request additional verification of nationality, visa status, and legal presence in Korea, and in practice, a foreigner without any Korean immigration record cannot complete the corporate representative verification. For capital escrow accounts under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a designated bank may accept the required documentation via a Korean law firm or notary, but the signatory must still attend a physical branch in-person to sign the account agreement and complete biometric identity verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner is a non-resident director with no Korean ARC, creating an unverifiable 'non-face-to-face' identity signature.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified copy of the director's valid foreign passport, a signed individual KYC questionnaire, a certificate of the company's overseas jurisdiction tax residency, a properly apostilled board resolution appointing the director as the account signatory, and a legalized copy of the director's visa or any valid Korean immigration record. If the director is not physically present, an irrevocable power of attorney in favor of a Korean resident agent, notarized at the Korean consulate, must be submitted, along with the agent's own ARC and fingerprint verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared business scope (financial portfolio tracking software) and payment flows from consumer subscriptions, which could be an indicator of unlicensed financial advisory activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the statutory corporate charter translated by a licensed Korean translator, a detailed business model white paper clarifying that the service is a data aggregation and tracking dashboard without any custodial, brokerage, or advisory function, an annual compliance opinion from a Korean law firm confirming that no financial license is required under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act or the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, and copies of signed SaaS terms of service and privacy policies governing user data handling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from an overseas source raises doubt about the economic substance and original source of funds, potentially triggering an unusual transaction report under the Financial Transaction Reports Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a three-month bank statement from the shareholder's home-currency account supporting the origin of the wire, the signed share subscription agreement, the Korean notary or law firm's audit of the capital increase resolution, the corporate registration certificate showing the paid-in capital, and a declaration of source of wealth signed by each non-resident shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring subscription revenues coupled with high chargeback expectations in the App Store and Play Store channels may be misclassified as high-risk virtual asset or gambling proceeds by the bank's automated scoring engine.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the executed Apple Developer Agreement and Google Play Payment Terms, a letter from the company's payment processor (e.g., Stripe) confirming the merchant category code (MCC) of 5734 for computer software stores or 8999 for professional services, a projected cash flow model seasonality report, and a compliance policy document outlining spend analytics and anti-fraud safeguards, all to be reviewed by the bank's transaction monitoring team.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial equity injection from foreign shareholders, the Cusik Hoesa must file a 'Report on Acquisition of Shares by a Foreigner' under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through the receiving bank (e.g., KB Kookmin or Hana Bank). The recommending bank will issue the 'Certificate of Reporting on Foreign Investment' after verifying the remittance. Stakeholder remittances must use SWIFT MT103 or equivalent with the purpose code '12500 – Foreign Direct Investment in Local Company' or the appropriate BOK Foreign Exchange Reporting purpose code 'K060'. Ample proof of the transaction prior to wiring is essential, including a notarized capital call resolution, a share issuance statement, and the company's corporate registration. The bank will verify the inflow against the foreign investment report and automatically credit the Capital Escrow Account (Invest-Sung Account). For any subsequent injections exceeding USD 10 million, the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Concentration and Administration Office must be notified in advance. The entire capital verification process typically takes 3-5 business days after the subscription amount is cleared, subject to no adverse media hits on the shareholder names.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments, including software royalties and intercompany service charges, should be executed via standard SWIFT MT103 message over the domestic bank's secure corporate e-banking channel. Each payment must be accompanied by an FX purchase application mentioning the appropriate BOK purpose code (e.g., 'D30 – Service Accounting: Software Maintenance' or 'A10 – Trade-Related Sales Commission'). For larger transactional flows exceeding USD 500,000 per occurrence, the bank may request the underlying contract, invoice, and English/Korean translation. For cross-border subscription revenue repatriation to the overseas parent or shareholder, the same MT103 method applies, but withholding tax clearances and treaty benefit certifications must be attached if treaty-exempt dividend rates are claimed. Commercial letters of credit (L/C) are not normally required for a pure software business unless the company is issuing licenses to Korean distributors under a structured off-take arrangement; in such case, a 'Supplier's Facility' L/C at sight or a Documentary Collection (D/P or D/A) can be opened through Hana Bank's or Shinhan Bank's trade finance division, with an underlying master license agreement and IRD (Importer's Remittance/Export Declaration) forms integrated into the bank's trade portal.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts (plain vanilla FX forwards) with a licensed Korean bank for hedging real commercial transactions denominated in USD/EUR or other foreign currencies, requiring evidence of underlying trade exposure such as invoices or subscription revenue forecasts.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offshore are only permissible for entities with valid underlying exposure and through a domestic bank's offshore affiliate, subject to BOK restriction that no netting arrangement creates a speculative position.

Currency swaps are permissible only when the company enters a cross-currency interest rate swap with a Korean bank for the purpose of converting an existing foreign-currency debt facility into KRW, and the notional amount must not exceed the principal of the underlying external borrowing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and approval of audited or unaudited financial statements, including balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, and cash flow statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial registration registry of the Supreme Court of Korea; retained in the corporate minute book and available for inspection by shareholders, courts, and the National Tax Service upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a fiscal year ending December 31, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM within the statutory window may expose the representative director to non-penal fines of up to KRW 10,000,000 under the Korean Commercial Act, and a shareholder may petition the court for a special inspection or judicial dissolution where the omission is persistent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return and final tax computation schedule, including local income tax attached return and any foreign investment related disclosures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar fiscal year, by March 31 of the following tax year; the interim tax prepayments due on August 31 and November 30 do not discharge the annual filing obligation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late or non-filed return incurs a negligence penalty of 20% of the underlying tax liability (reduced to 10% for voluntary correction submitted after the due date but before NTS notice), plus daily overdue interest of 0.022% from the original due date; where the tax remains unpaid for three months after the due date, the NTS may seize operating accounts and may administratively nullify the corporate business registration for procurement and trade licensing purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements, if the company exceeds the mandatory external audit threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART disclosure system, with a service copy to the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within fourteen days after the certified auditor delivers the report and in all events before the statutory AGM approval date; for a December 31 year-end company, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the external audit report or to appoint an independent auditor may trigger an administrative surcharge of up to KRW 30,000,000 on the representative director, a corrective order from the FSS, and referral to the Serious Financial Crime Investigation Bureau in respect of any materially false statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise report and foreign exchange position declaration, but only when non-resident shareholders hold at least 10% of the issued shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA and the Foreign Exchange Information System operated with the Bank of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On an annual basis by March 31 for the prior calendar year, with a 30-day post-closing report required for any new share purchase by a non-resident
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing may result in administrative fines up to KRW 20,000,000 under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and dividend remittances through domestic banks may be blocked until a compliant declaration is accepted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a mandatory independent certified public accountant audit is legally required for a Chusik Hoesa if: (i) total assets as at the preceding fiscal year-end exceed KRW 10 billion; or (ii) total assets exceed KRW 7 billion and either annual revenue exceeds KRW 30 billion or the average number of employees is at least 300; or (iii) the company is listed on a Korean or foreign securities exchange; or (iv) the Financial Services Commission designates the company as requiring external audit in the public interest. In addition, a shareholder or shareholder group holding at least 5% of issued shares may demand a special audit under Article 4 of the same Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for any entity above the compulsory audit threshold and for listed or public-interest entities; Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) and the Korea SMEs Accounting Standards are available for companies below the threshold that are not otherwise required to adopt K-IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not currently impose a generic public annual UBO register for private Chusik Hoesa entities. However, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act mandates a 30-day post-closing report to the competent bank or KOTRA whenever a non-resident acquires, directly or indirectly, 10% or more of the shares or voting rights. Domestically, the board must confirm the register of members before each annual general meeting, and any change in major shareholders must be recorded in the corporate minute book. For foreign-owned entities, an annual confirmation of the foreign investment status must be submitted to KOTRA or the reporting bank by March 31 of the following year. No additional government filing is required for a wholly domestic private company unless a reportable transfer takes place.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,800 per annum for a standard registered office and corporate secretarial agent arrangement in Seoul, including bilingual compliance support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 15,000 per annum for a small or middle-market fintech software entity, depending on transaction volume, intercompany flows, and the complexity of the financial portfolio tracking system.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: National Corporate Income Tax of 24% on taxable income above KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surcharge, giving a top aggregate statutory rate of 26.4%; lower brackets are 9%, 19% and 21% for income up to KRW 200 million, KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion respectively
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D expenditure tax credits for qualifying software and fintech development under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; Free Economic Zone and Foreign Investment Zone incentives including a 50% corporate income tax reduction for the first three years for qualifying foreign-invested high-tech entities; possible SME reduced rates and integrated investment tax credits; no general patent-box regime for internally developed software

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1 Corporate Income Tax Return submitted through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal, with the annual International Transactions Summary attached when cross-border related-party transactions exceed the statutory threshold
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with semi-annual estimated intermediate tax payments for a corporation with a December 31 fiscal year-end
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year corporation the filing deadline is March 31 of the following tax year; a limited extension of up to one month may be granted by the National Tax Service only for extraordinary circumstances

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income amount, after adding taxable income adjustments and deducting loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with a Korean permanent establishment must include Korean-source business income attributable to the PE, including subscription fees, Apple IAP/Stripe commissions and portfolio-tracking service revenue; offshore income sourced outside Korea must be excluded unless effectively connected with the Korean PE; maintain contemporaneous revenue records in KRW

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculated by applying the progressive national tax rates to the taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the graduated rate table carefully and add the 10% local income tax surcharge on the resulting national tax; treaty provisions do not reduce the national corporate income tax itself; a non-resident PE should document the local income tax separately in the return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, exemptions and tax credits, including the R&D credit, foreign tax credit and treaty-related reductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits for which the Korean PE is the beneficial user; do not claim a deduction for royalties paid to an offshore affiliate unless the payment satisfies the arm's-length standard and Korean economic substance requirements; attach foreign tax credit statements and any approved treaty forms

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts already paid, including intermediate tax installments, withheld taxes and advance payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Korean-source withholding taxes suffered on interest, royalties and service income, plus any semi-annual estimated payments will be credited here; retain official receipts and withholding certificates because the National Tax Service will verify the credits before refund or assessment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refundable after crediting prepayments and withholding
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance must be paid by the statutory deadline; a non-resident PE claiming a refund must have filed the return timely, maintain Korean bank account details and secure a completion of the National Tax Service refund review; late payment of the balance triggers daily late-payment surcharge plus possible criminal exposure if omitted intentionally

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and unfaithful declaration penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-2 and 47-3 include 10%-20% of the underpaid tax for negligence, up to 40% for fraudulent understatement, plus statutory daily late-payment surcharge; failure to file altogether attracts an additional 20% penalty on the unpaid tax; willful tax evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evasion and Tax Offenses Act with imprisonment for up to five years or fines up to five times the evaded tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder, plus 10% local income tax surcharge, making the aggregate statutory rate 22%; treaty rates may reduce the dividend WHT to 5%, 10% or 15% depending on shareholding, treaty and beneficial ownership; a Korean branch paying dividends to its foreign head office is treated separately as branch remittance tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To access reduced DTA rates, the beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its home jurisdiction and submit the Application for Reduction or Exemption of Non-resident Withholding Tax under a Tax Treaty to the Korean withholding agent before payment; the filing must include a statement of beneficial ownership, shareholding history and proof that the recipient is not a conduit; the withholding agent reports the treaty treatment on the payment withholding return and retains all documents; if the documentation is not complete, the statutory 22% rate must be withheld and a refund or adjustment may be pursued within the statutory limitation period; branch remittance tax relief also requires a treaty claim and CRS/residency declarations
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory aggregate withholding on cross-border interest and royalties is 22% for a non-resident foreign corporation; bilateral treaties commonly reduce interest to 0%-15% and royalties to 10%-15% depending on the jurisdiction, article and beneficial ownership; for the ISIC 6201 software/portfolio-tracking business, payments for a fintech platform license or data subscription are frequently characterized as royalties, so the payer must analyze Korean sourcing rules, PE exposure and treaty characterization before applying a reduced rate

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50,000,000,000 of aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in a fiscal year triggers the mandatory preparation and submission of Master File and Local File transfer pricing documentation; additional simplified documentation or an International Transactions Summary may be required even below this threshold when requested by the National Tax Service
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes incorporates a strong substance-over-form doctrine; a Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in personal wealth analytics and investment tracking must prove that its Core Income-Generating Activities, including software development, data custody, user contracting, risk management and strategic decision-making, are genuinely performed by Korean employees and management; the National Tax Service and the Financial Intelligence Unit will disregard a paper entity that cannot demonstrate such substance and may apply controlled foreign company rules and treaty abuse defenses

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by False or Omitted Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A director causes the Chusik Hoesa to file a Corporate Income Tax Return that deliberately understates subscription or IAP revenue, fabricates deductions, or omits foreign financial portfolio gains while transferring profits to related foreign shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evasion and Tax Offenses Act Articles 10 and 12; Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-2 and 47-3; penalties include 20%-40% of underpaid tax, statutory daily late-payment surcharge, criminal fines up to five times the evaded tax and imprisonment for up to five years; the National Tax Service may also issue a demand for restitution of the evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean Commercial Act Article 401 permits third parties to pierce the corporate veil and hold directors jointly and severally liable for damages caused by intentional or grossly negligent breaches of duty; a director who signs a knowingly false return loses limited liability, may suffer personal asset seizure, be placed on a National Tax Service blacklist, be subject to a travel ban, and be criminally imprisoned

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity pays excessive royalties or service fees to an offshore software parent, undertakes no arm's-length benchmarking, and fails to prepare Master File or Local File documentation even though cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 50,000,000,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of International Taxes Act Articles 5, 6, 11 and 12; the National Tax Service may adjust taxable income to the arm's-length range, impose an additional tax of 20%-40% on the understated tax, and levy fixed administrative penalties for missing or false transfer pricing documentation; unconscious noncompliance also impairs the availability of corresponding adjustments and treaty mutual agreement procedure relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve non-arm's-length contracts or false documentation may be personally liable for the resulting tax deficiencies under Commercial Act Article 401; a court may disregard the corporate entity if the transactions lack economic substance, exposing the director's personal assets and triggering criminal sanctions under the tax evasion laws, including imprisonment and travel restrictions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chusik Hoesa is incorporated with no Korean employees, no office, no actual board meetings and no core income-generating activity in Korea, and is used as a conduit to hold foreign financial portfolios or route interest, dividends and royalties to nominee non-resident shareholders without reporting the foreign investment to the Korean authorities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14 allows recharacterization of sham transactions; Adjustment of International Taxes Act Article 17 imposes controlled foreign company rules on the Korean beneficial owners; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act violations carry administrative fines and potential criminal penalties; the National Tax Service may assess corporate income tax, local income tax and penalty taxes on the substance owner and cancel any benefit obtained through the shell
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the corporate form is only a sham, courts may lift the veil and hold directors personally liable for restitution of taxes, interest and penalties; directors face seizure of personal assets, blacklisting by the National Tax Service, travel bans, and criminal imprisonment for intentional fraud or violation of foreign exchange reporting obligations; the limitation of liability characteristic of a Chusik Hoesa is lost when the director personally participates in the misuse of the corporate form
